findings.title: PUMS information conflated with coarse benchmark recode
findings.source_claim: Multi-race Census answers are simplified into single-label categories in ACS PUMS; this is invoked as a data-availability obstacle.
findings.suspect_step: Generalizing RAC1P-only task encoding to the full microdata schema
findings.check: 2022 PUMS metadata exposes independent RACWHT/RACBLK/RACASN yes/no combination-aware indicators alongside RAC1P. Static ACSIncome definition uses group='RAC1P'.
findings.alternative_reading: True as a narrower statement about a RAC1P-only benchmark export.
findings.supported_impact: Local practical premise incorrect; no demonstrated failure of normative thesis

repair.statement: Distinguish RAC1P-based benchmark collapse from separate race indicators available in ACS PUMS
repair.verification: Verified against official metadata; no empirical fairness improvement claimed

findings.remaining_work: Human decision on wording; no original experiment claimed to be repaired

findings.title: Survey ledger and inclusion criteria not independently reconcilable
findings.source_claim: 78 screened papers,45 group fairness papers,29 racial-category papers; AppendixA states28
findings.check: Table1 has37 citations and26 distinct author-year entries; includes Xu/Strohmer2023 identified in JMLR24(331)
findings.alternative_reading: Omitted rows, stale count or wrong citation could explain differences
findings.supported_impact: Survey auditability limited; direction and magnitude of any corrected prevalence unknown

repair.verification: Not possible without original screening/coding ledger

findings.remaining_work: Obtain the full78/45/29 ledger and mapping to table;26 must not replace29 as prevalence numerator

scope_clarifications.statement: Subgroup fairness can operate over arbitrary protected feature vectors and group indicator families; categorical race is an instantiation, not a formal prerequisite.
scope_clarifications.counterevidence: Kearns2018 empirical features include census-derived racial information, supporting a narrower reading.
